svg.title: Kafka lost nothing. The application's own memory of what it had already added up did.
svg.desc: A plain KafkaConsumer loop keeps a revenue-by-zone tally in an ordinary Python dictionary. Run 1 processes 30,000 real trip events and tallies $711,532.04 in memory, then the process ends. Run 2 starts fresh, correctly resumes from Kafka's own committed offset with zero messages lost or repeated, and tallies its own $676,671.90 -- with no memory of run 1's total. Kafka guaranteed the messages; nothing guaranteed the aggregate built from them. The true combined total, $1,388,203.94, exists nowhere.
svg.text: process ends -- dict is gone with it
a fresh dict, in a fresh process
correctly resumed -- zero knowledge of run 1
exists in neither process's memory -- computed here only by adding the two prints together
Kafka's own offsets were never wrong. The application's memory of its own math was.
This is the exact gap a stream processor's stateful tables exist to close
